messages:
maria: heads up — saw a flakey case in the python async client where we keep getting 429s even though the quota header says remaining=1. logs attached below.

jon: hmm. can you paste the raw headers? sometimes our header-normalization logic lowercases keys on sync but not on async responses.

maria: pasted excerpt from the failing run:

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-Redwood-Quota-Limit: 100
X-Redwood-Quota-Remaining: 0
X-Redwood-Quota-Reset: 1718000000
content-type: application/json

{"id":"resp-123"}
```

maria: but the client log shows remaining=1 right before the request is sent. then we get a 429 and the retry window calc is tiny (like 0s).

sam: that sounds like a race between our client-side quota cache and the header parser. async path updates the in-memory token-bucket from response headers, but there's an await point where another coro fires off a request reading the stale bucket.

lee: aka two coroutines read->decide->send while the first hasn't written the header-updated value back. we need an atomic update or a queue for throttle checks.

jon: agreed. quick mitigation: treat the server quota headers as authoritative on 200/2xx responses and on 429 pulls the Retry-After. For concurrency we can use an asyncio.Lock per client instance around read-modify-write of the bucket counters. cheap and effective.

maria: ok I can prototype a lock. question: what about when headers are missing (some proxied requests strip vendor headers)? current code assumes header keys always present and casts to int. that blew up in another test.

qa: repro steps I used: run load test with 50 coros, short sequence length. sometimes the header comes back on 200 but not on 429, and sometimes the header is lowercased by the test proxy (`x-redwood-quota-remaining`). client currently does headers.get('X-Redwood-Quota-Remaining') only.

sam: we should normalize header keys case-insensitively. use response.headers.get('x-redwood-quota-remaining') or better: iterate dict with lowercased keys on parse. also defensively handle missing values with fallback to None and not crash.

jon: also add a conservative safety margin when remaining==0: if we see remaining===0, set local bucket to 0 and block until reset_ts + 1. compute reset from header but defend if reset is absent — use Date header + Retry-After or fallback to exponential backoff.

maria: proposed minimal diff (pseudo):

```py
async with self._quota_lock:
    hdrs = {k.lower(): v for k, v in resp.headers.items()}
    rem = hdrs.get('x-redwood-quota-remaining')
    if rem is not None:
        try:
            self._bucket.remaining = max(0, int(rem))
        except ValueError:
            logger.warning('malformed quota header: %r', rem)
    reset = hdrs.get('x-redwood-quota-reset')
    # convert epoch or iso -> set self._bucket.reset_ts
```

sam: looks good. add a small unit test that spawns two coros that both call .acquire() concurrently and assert only one proceeds when remaining=1.

lee: also file a follow-up to update the sync client to have parity (we had slightly different header names historically). we should have a shared parser util so both clients behave identically.

qa: I'll add the integration test that uses a small proxy to simulate missing/lowercased headers and intermittent 429s. can we also log the header parse errors as a metric? would help ops.

maria: I'll open a draft PR with the lock + parser util + tests. tagging you @jon @sam for review.

ci-bot: build queued for PR #4567 — unit tests running.

jon: nice. one more nit — when computing retry window from reset header, round up to the next second and add a +1 safety to avoid zero windows; I hit flakes because reset and server time were slightly misaligned.

maria: noted. will include. thanks all :thumbsup:
